Chapter 09 of 19

The Repair People

Repair / InterfereEast Van / citywide120 BPM
The story

Terminal City is always coming apart a little. Cracks open, colours fade, and pieces of the day go missing. The people who keep it together are the Repair People: graffiti writers, painters, sticker makers, muralists, photographers, paste-up crews, and anyone with a marker and a ladder.

What ordinary Vancouver calls a tag, a mural, a poster or a sticker is, in Terminal City, structural maintenance. A painted line across a crack is holding the wall together. A sticker on a pole is patching a leak in the day. The layers pile up because no repair lasts forever, and the next crew always has more to fix.

Many of their ideas come back from the Green Static, where nothing is authorized and everything is new. Even the Probes down at the port carry repair marks. The Repair People have one rule, and it is strict: never paint over something you did not see being painted. Mark the wall. Patch the crack. Still wet. Hold it together.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
